name: Karma Police
memo: Radiohead - Karma Police: acoustic-style strummed rhythm (Thom Yorke) with piano-like space; clean, warm, light room reverb. Approximation.

band.style_feel: slow, laid-back straight eighths, soft kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, sparse in the verses
band.key: ambiguous: usually given as G major; Wikipedia reads the verse as A minor/Dorian (or E minor/Phrygian)
parts: Part A: verse - acoustic strum and piano, quiet drums
Part B: 'This is what you get' chorus - drums and bass enter, fuller
Part C: 'For a minute there' section - build
Part D: outro - feedback delay noise, drums out
band.tips: Tempo is about 75 BPM (sources say 73-76; some count it double-time at 150). Strum steady eighths for 2 bars before the Trio+ starts learning; key sources disagree, so go by the chords (Am, Bm, C, Em, G, D, F).

whammy.tuning: Standard (E A D G B E)
whammy.tips: Standard tuning; no whammy or octave effect is documented on the recording. The closing 'melting' sound is a delay pushed into feedback, not a pitch effect.

originals.guitar: Yairi DY-88 acoustic (live on the OK Computer tour; studio use not confirmed)

guitar.position: neck or middle pickup for the strum, tone around 7
guitar.tone_notes: The song is built on a strummed acoustic with piano; an electric on a clean, warm setting works. Roll treble back a little for a rounder sound.

name: Karma Outro
memo: Radiohead - Karma Police: ending. Ed O'Brien's delay pushed into self-oscillation (DMX 15-80S); turn the delay level/feedback up by hand for the 'melting' wash.
